To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the New Work approach, which is characterized by flat hierarchies and self-organization, is not sufficient to create a sense of meaning and belonging among employees.

(1) the implementation of agile working practices and the introduction of flat hierarchies and self-organization are not sufficient to overcome hierarchical structures and group dynamics in organizations, (2) the implementation of new work practices and the use of self-organized structures do not necessarily lead to a reduction of complexity and the resolution of problems, (3) the implementation of New Work practices and the use self-organized structures does not necessarily lead to the creation of a sense of belonging and empowerment among employees,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether the implementation of new working structures in agile organizations leads to the expected results in terms of employee motivation, satisfaction and commitment.
the question of how employees in the context of agile working experience the meaning and bonding.
the question of how to understand the experience of meaning, belonging and personal empowerment in New Work environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
New Work and agile work structures are not able to replace the need for human relationships and social dynamics, but rather need them in order to be effective.
the New Work approach is an attempt to create a more humane and sustainable working environment by means of a more flexible and agile organization.
New Work is not a panacea for the future, but rather a set of tools that can be applied to the future of work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the New Work movement is not only a new way of work but a movement of a whole generation of employees.
New Work is a complex and multi-faceted concept that is still in development.
the implementation of New Work is a complex task, which requires the integration of different perspectives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current New Work approaches are not sufficient to meet the needs of the new generation of employees.
the current hype of new work is not a new work, but an old work with a new name.

the current state of the art in agile work practices does not seem to be able to deliver what it is supposed to deliver, i.e. to create a new, self-determined and meaningful work culture that fosters a high degree of employee autonomy and empowerment.
